title: Seven Lines of Code: Stripe's Developer-First Revolution
description: Payment integration takes weeks and requires talking to salespeople. You believe it should take 7 lines of code. Build the payment infrastructure for the internet.
learningObjectives: Creating a platform vs a product
backstory: Patrick and John Collison tried to accept payments for their startups and were shocked by how terrible the experience was. PayPal took 2 weeks to activate accounts. Traditional payment processors required talking to sales reps, signing contracts, and weeks of integration. They thought: this should be as easy as any other API.

realWorldInspiration.outcome: Started with '/v1/charges' API endpoint. Now processes $640B+ annually. Valued at $95B. Powers millions of businesses globally.

decisions.description: You're building payment infrastructure. Who should you optimize for: developers, businesses, or merchants?

options.label: Build for Developers First
options.description: Create the best API developers have ever used. Make integration take minutes, not weeks. Perfect documentation. No sales calls required.

immediate.eventDescription: You obsess over API design. Every error message is helpful. Docs include code samples for 8 languages. Stripe.js makes PCI compliance invisible.

longTerm.eventDescription: Developers love you! They're integrating Stripe in their side projects, then bringing it to their day jobs. Word spreads on Hacker News.

analysis.reasoning: Stripe's secret: developers are the decision makers at tech companies. Win them, and they'll pull your product into their companies. Product-led growth.
analysis.realWorldExample: Stripe's documentation became legendary. Developers would integrate Stripe just to learn good API design.

advisorCommentary.comment: Developer experience is your moat. If integration takes 10 minutes instead of 2 weeks, you win by default.
Developers are vocal influencers. Make them love you and they'll be your unpaid marketing army.

options.label: Target Enterprise Businesses
options.description: Go after big companies with enterprise sales. They have money and need payment processing.

immediate.eventDescription: You hire enterprise sales reps. Sales cycles are 9-18 months. You're building custom features for each prospect.

longTerm.eventDescription: You land a few enterprise deals, but it's slow and capital-intensive. Your product is becoming bloated with custom features.

analysis.reasoning: Enterprise sales is slow and expensive. Meanwhile, developer-focused competitors are growing exponentially through word-of-mouth.

advisorCommentary.comment: Enterprise sales burns cash fast. If one deal falls through, your metrics crater.

options.label: Focus on Small Merchants
options.description: Build a Square-like experience for physical retail. Card readers, POS systems, easy onboarding.

immediate.eventDescription: You're competing with Square in a crowded market. Hardware is expensive. Support costs are high.

analysis.reasoning: Physical retail is a different business - lower margins, higher support costs, commodity market. You're missing the internet commerce opportunity.

advisorCommentary.comment: You're playing someone else's game. Square already won physical retail. What's your unique advantage?

decisions.description: A developer wants to integrate Stripe. Current payment processors require: 1) Sales call, 2) Paperwork, 3) 2-week review, 4) Complex integration. What's your approach?

options.label: Instant Signup, Live in Minutes
options.description: Sign up with email. Get API keys instantly. Make first test transaction in 7 lines of code. No sales calls. Ever.

immediate.eventDescription: Developers are shocked. 'Wait, that's it?' They integrate Stripe into hackathon projects. Screenshots of your simple API go viral.

longTerm.eventDescription: Word spreads like wildfire. YC startups all use Stripe. Then they grow and bring Stripe with them. Viral growth loop established.

analysis.reasoning: This is Stripe's breakthrough innovation. Removing friction from signup creates viral adoption. The best product is the easiest to try.
analysis.realWorldExample: Stripe.js library became the gold standard. Developers integrated it 'just to try' and never switched back.

advisorCommentary.comment: You've eliminated every excuse not to try your product. That's how you create exponential growth.
Perfect product-led growth. Users activate themselves. Your CAC is near zero.

options.label: Quick Vetting Process (48 hours)
options.description: Require basic business info, run quick checks, approve in 48 hours. Balanced approach between speed and safety.

immediate.eventDescription: The vetting slows adoption. Developers who want to integrate right now go to competitors with instant signup.

longTerm.eventDescription: You have fewer fraud issues, but you're losing the viral growth race. Developers talk about your competitor, not you.

analysis.reasoning: Every hour of friction kills conversion. In developer tools, the faster path wins. Handle fraud with technology, not process.

advisorCommentary.comment: You're letting fear of fraud slow your growth. Build better fraud detection instead of adding friction.

decisions.description: Instant signup is working great, but you're seeing fraud. $50K in fraudulent transactions last month. Investors are worried. What do you do?

options.label: Build ML-Powered Fraud Detection
options.description: Invest heavily in machine learning. Detect fraud algorithmically without slowing signups. Make it a product advantage.

immediate.eventDescription: You hire ML engineers and build Radar - a fraud detection system. Initial results are promising.

longTerm.eventDescription: Radar becomes industry-leading. You're blocking fraud better than anyone while maintaining instant signup. It becomes a selling point.

analysis.reasoning: Stripe's actual approach: turn fraud prevention into a competitive advantage. Radar became a product that merchants would pay extra for.
analysis.realWorldExample: Stripe Radar now blocks billions in fraud annually using ML. It's a major product offering, not just a cost center.

advisorCommentary.comment: Perfect technical solution. You're solving the problem at scale, not adding process bandaids.
You turned a problem into a feature. That's product thinking at its best.

options.label: Add Manual Review Process
options.description: Review all new accounts manually. Flag suspicious patterns. Slower but safer.

immediate.eventDescription: You hire reviewers. Fraud decreases but signup time goes to 24-48 hours. Growth slows dramatically.

longTerm.eventDescription: You've lost your main advantage: instant signup. Developers complain. Competitors with better tech are winning.

analysis.reasoning: Manual processes don't scale. You're sacrificing your competitive advantage (speed) for a short-term fix.

advisorCommentary.comment: You just killed the golden goose. Your differentiation was instant signup. Now you're just another payment processor.

options.label: Require Business Verification
options.description: Make users verify their business before going live. EIN numbers, business licenses, etc.

immediate.eventDescription: Growth grinds to a halt. Developers trying to build side projects can't use you. You're now optimized for established businesses only.

analysis.reasoning: You just became the enemy you set out to disrupt. Verification requirements kill the 'seven lines of code' promise.

advisorCommentary.comment: You let fear turn you into the thing you were disrupting. Your users wanted simplicity, you gave them complexity.
